key_insight: The paper proposes reducing the separation between modalities by changing the geometry of their shared embedding space—from a unit sphere to a probability simplex. The simplex constrains every embedding to nonnegative values that sum to one.
problem_solved: Multimodal contrastive models such as CLIP and CLAP can learn a shared representation space while still placing different modalities in separate regions—a persistent 'modality gap.'
method: Replace unit-sphere embeddings with probability-simplex embeddings.
Use nonnegativity and unit-sum constraints as a structural prior for shared representations.
Change the embedding geometry while preserving its intrinsic dimension.
impact: This offers practitioners a geometry-based approach to improving cross-modal alignment. The supplied abstract is truncated and reports no experimental results, so performance gains cannot be assessed from it.
visual_elements: Before-and-after schematic: separated modality clusters versus the intended cross-modal alignment.
Sphere-to-simplex diagram showing the proposed change in embedding domain.
Constraint graphic: nonnegative coordinates whose values sum to one.
Image, text, and audio icons feeding into a shared simplex representation.
paper_title: Closing the Modality Gap via Simplex-Constrained Representations
paper_authors: Shubham Gupta, Siva Reddy, Perouz Taslakian, Valentina Zantedeschi, Cem Subakan
